slides.label: Title
slides.notes: Open the lecture by saying that self-duality is a four-dimensional accident that becomes a structural tool. The chapter is not just about a special curvature equation; it is about how orientation, conformal geometry, complex geometry, and Einstein metrics meet in dimension four.

slides.label: Four Dimensions
slides.notes: Emphasize the dimension count before any theorem is stated. In four dimensions, two-forms have the same rank on both sides of the Hodge star, so the star operator has eigenspaces rather than merely moving forms to a different degree. This is the algebraic doorway into self-duality.

slides.label: Hodge Splitting
slides.notes: Walk through the picture as a pointwise linear algebra statement on an oriented Euclidean four-space. The decomposition is not a choice of coordinates after the metric and orientation are fixed. The plus and minus halves are the two possible signs of the star action.

slides.label: Curvature Matrix
slides.notes: Present the Riemann curvature tensor as a symmetric operator on two-forms. This block matrix is the organizing object for the lecture: scalar curvature, traceless Ricci curvature, and the two Weyl halves all have visible locations. Students should remember where each piece sits, not just its name.

slides.label: Weyl Halves
slides.notes: Define half-conformal flatness through the vanishing of one Weyl block. The term self-dual is convention-dependent because reversing orientation swaps the labels plus and minus. The geometric content is the disappearance of one conformal curvature half.

slides.label: Orientation
slides.notes: Use this slide to prevent a common error. A metric alone does not decide which Weyl half is called self-dual; the chosen orientation does. The underlying curvature may be the same while the plus and minus labels exchange.

slides.label: Conformal Invariance
slides.notes: Stress that the Weyl tensor is the conformal curvature, so self-duality is naturally a conformal condition. Rescaling the metric changes lengths and scalar quantities, but the vanishing of a Weyl half is preserved. This is why twistor methods can enter a chapter in an Einstein manifolds course.

slides.label: Example Taxonomy
slides.notes: This slide is a map rather than a classification theorem. The point is to separate three ideas that are easy to blur: conformal flatness, half-conformal flatness, and Einstein curvature. Some important examples sit at intersections, while other metrics satisfy only one part of the story.

slides.label: Einstein Simplification
slides.notes: The Einstein condition removes the off-diagonal traceless Ricci block in the curvature operator. That does not force either Weyl half to vanish, but it makes the block picture cleaner and turns self-dual Einstein metrics into a sharply constrained class. This is one reason the chapter belongs in the course.

slides.label: Topological Bookkeeping
slides.notes: Introduce the formulas as global accounting identities rather than as local definitions. Curvature integrals remember Euler characteristic and signature, and the two Weyl halves contribute asymmetrically to the signature. The identities explain why self-duality has topological consequences.

slides.label: Twistor Space
slides.notes: Describe twistor space as the bundle of compatible complex structures on tangent spaces. Over each point of the oriented four-manifold sits a two-sphere of possible complex structures. The self-duality equation is precisely what makes the natural almost complex structure on this bundle integrable.

slides.label: Penrose Direction
slides.notes: The Penrose construction turns a self-dual conformal four-manifold into complex geometry. Fibers become rational curves with controlled normal bundle, and real structure remembers the original real manifold. The important lecture move is that curvature information has become holomorphic incidence data.

slides.label: Reverse Penrose
slides.notes: Now reverse the arrows carefully. Starting from suitable complex data, one recovers a real four-manifold as a moduli space of rational curves. The hypotheses are not decoration; they are what ensure that the recovered space has the right dimension, real form, and self-dual conformal structure.

slides.label: Einstein Applications
slides.notes: Explain that the Einstein condition adds extra structure to the twistor space, often visible through contact or symplectic data depending on the scalar curvature regime. This is where the chapter links forward to quaternion-Kahler geometry. The deck should leave students expecting the next chapter rather than treating twistor theory as isolated.

slides.label: Failure Modes
slides.notes: Use this warning slide to catch three mistakes. First, self-dual is not the same as Ricci-flat. Second, changing orientation changes which half vanishes. Third, a formal-looking twistor space does not reconstruct the geometry unless the incidence and real-structure hypotheses are satisfied.

slides.label: Learner Lab
slides.notes: Turn the lecture into a small inspection exercise. Students should be able to place a given curvature operator into the block diagram, identify whether the Einstein simplification occurs, and decide which Weyl half would need to vanish. The last prompt asks them to translate the same decision into twistor language.

slides.label: Recap
slides.notes: Close by tying the algebraic and geometric pictures together. The Hodge star creates the two halves, the Weyl tensor records the conformal obstruction, and twistor space repackages self-duality as integrability. The Einstein condition then supplies the bridge to the next chapter on quaternion-Kahler manifolds.
